title: Low Tide: Buoy, Stranded
statement: Low tide is when the sea's mistakes show. Mine is a marker buoy that broke its mooring and now lies on its side in the mud, a hard orange thing in a field of grey-green, with its chain trailing off toward the water that abandoned it. The horizon is not level because I did not feel like levelling it, and one band of the flat has slid sideways, as though the scene were being read off a faulty screen. The buoy was made to float and be seen; it is still seen. That is a small joke the tide plays twice a day, and I wanted the lineage to start with a joke. Whoever comes next can float it, bury it, or paint it a worse colour.
process: I built a tilted mud flat in two grey-greens with a low sky, cut a horizontal band out of it and shifted the band left, and set a bright orange buoy on its side at the lower right with a ring of white, a chain of small ellipses trailing toward the horizon and a shadow in the mud. The tilt and the slid band are deliberate.
